newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo Jan-April tourism down 17.8 pct on 1996-stats.
newsitem.headline: Yugo Jan-April tourism down 17.8 pct on 1996-stats.

text.p: Yugoslavia registered a total of 623,606 tourists in the January-April period, a drop of 17.8 percent against the same period last year, the Federal Statistics Office reported on Friday.
Yugoslavs numbered 550,059 of the total, down 18.7 percent on January-April 1996.
Visitors from other former Yugoslav republics -- Bosnia, Croatia, Macedonia and Slovenia -- totalled 35,717, a drop of 7.8 percent.
The number of foreign tourists also dropped 12.7 percent against the same period last year to 37,830.
Most foreign visitors came from Italy (5,239), followed by Germany (3,284), Bulgaria (3,105), Greece (3,054), Austria (2,445) and the Russian Federation (2,218).
According to data of the National Bank of Yugoslavia, hard currency income from tourism in January-March 1997 totalled $6.9 million, down 11.5 percent compared to the same three-month period in 1996.
NOTE -- Data is based on reception figures from hotels and other accommodation facilities. -- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305
